tutorial.step1.intro: Morning. I'm Admiral Biscuit, your navigator. Find the wheel. Walk with WASD, press E at the helm.
Admiral Biscuit, decorated navigator. Don't ask about the incident. Wheel's at the back. E to grab it.
tutorial.step1.hint: The wheel. Round thing. Back of the boat. You walked past it.
Aft. That means the back. The wheel is aft.
tutorial.step1.done: Good. Hands on the wheel. Try not to look so pleased.
tutorial.step2.intro: That strip up top is the compass. Steer to ninety degrees. East. Hold it ten seconds.
A and D steer. Get the compass on 090, that's east, and keep it there.
tutorial.step2.hint: Small corrections. The boat takes a moment to answer. Like you.
Compass card, top of the view. Red mark on 090. Gently.
tutorial.step2.done: Steady on east. Compasses lie a degree or two, by the way. Iron aboard.
Ten seconds on a heading. Columbus is shaking.
tutorial.step3.intro: The sail's flapping. That's called luffing. W sheets it in, S eases it out.
Hear that flapping? Wasted wind. Sheet in with W until it fills.
tutorial.step3.hint: Flapping means too loose. Too tight and you stall. Find the middle.
Sheet in until the flapping stops, then a touch more. Not a lot more.
tutorial.step3.done: Now we're sailing. Fastest with the wind on the side. Never straight into it.
Lovely. Wind on the beam, sail drawing. Even I'm mildly impressed.
tutorial.step4.intro: Night falls. Faster than usual. Look north and find the Big Dipper.
Stars are out. Seven bright ones shaped like a saucepan, to the north. Find them.
tutorial.step4.hint: North. Behind you, probably. Look up a bit. Saucepan with a bent handle.
Seven stars. Four make a bowl, three make a handle. North sky.
tutorial.step4.done: That's the Big Dipper. Remember it. You'll need it more than you need me.
The Dipper. Ursa Major if you're posh. I am posh.
tutorial.step5.intro: The two stars at the end of the bowl are the pointers. Follow them about five times their gap.
Bowl's outer edge, two stars. Draw a line through them, away from the bowl. Keep going.
tutorial.step5.hint: No, the other end of the bowl. Yes. Keep going. Further. There.
I've drawn it for you. Don't tell anyone.
tutorial.step5.done: Polaris. It barely moves all night. Its height above the horizon is your latitude.
That's Polaris, the North Star. Not the brightest. Just the most useful. Like me.
tutorial.step6.intro: Right-click to hold out your fist. Bottom on the horizon. Count fists up to Polaris.
Arm out, fist on the horizon. One fist is ten degrees, one finger two. Measure Polaris.
tutorial.step6.hint: Hold right-click. Look at Polaris. Count the fists from the sea up to it.
Fists from the horizon. Not from your feet. The horizon.
tutorial.step6.ask: Well? How high is Polaris, and where does that put us?
tutorial.step6.wrong: No. Count again. Fist is ten, finger is two. I'll wait. I'm good at waiting.
Wrong. Polaris height equals latitude. Fists, then fingers. Again.
tutorial.step6.done: Correct. Polaris height is your latitude. Sailors used this for a thousand years.
Right. Twelve north, give or take. I knew that already, but well done.
tutorial.step9.intro: We're crossing the equator. Tradition says I insult you now. Consider it done.
Crossing the line. Sailors used to get dunked for this. You get me instead.
tutorial.step9.polaris: Polaris is below the horizon now. It's not hiding from you. Well. It is now.
South of the equator the North Star sets for good. New trick needed.
tutorial.step9.cross: Look south. Four bright stars in a kite. The Southern Cross. Two bright Pointers beside it.
South sky: a small cross, with two bright stars pointing at it. Find it.
tutorial.step9.crossHint: South. Low-ish. Smaller than you expect. Everyone says that.
If it has no pointers, it's the False Cross. The real one's tighter.
tutorial.step9.crossDone: That's Crux. The long bar points to the south pole. There's no star there. Just the spot.
Good. Now extend the long axis, top to foot, about four and a half lengths.
tutorial.step9.poleHint: Long bar, top star through the bright foot star. Keep going down. Four and a half times.
I've drawn the line. The pole is empty sky. Navigators found it anyway.
tutorial.step9.done: That empty patch is the south pole. Its height is your latitude south. Same trick, no star.
Found nothing, precisely. Its height above the horizon is how far south we are.
tutorial.end: Lesson over. Here come your first real orders.
That's the lot. Real orders now. Latitude first, then run it down.
log.thrown: Log line's out. Counting the knots against the sandglass.
Paying out the log. Sandglass running.
log.result: There's your speed. Plus or minus a sailor's honesty.
Speed logged. The chart will reckon our position from it. Roughly.
irons: We're pointing into the wind. That's called being in irons. Turn.
Nobody sails straight into the wind. Not even me.
luff.long: That flapping is money leaving the boat. Sheet in.
The sail is applauding your trim. Sarcastically.
south.lookingForPolaris: It's below the horizon. It's not hiding from you. Well. It is now.
chart.first: The chart. It shows where we think we are. Thinking is doing a lot of work there.
Our reckoned position. Compass, log and hope.
reef.hit: You hit a reef. In fairness, it was there first.
That noise was the hull. Reefs have a gap. Find it.
aground: We're on the beach. Boats go on water. Back off.
Aground. Very efficient way to stop.
island.arrive: Land. Check it against the description before you start bragging.
An island. Is it the right one? Look at its shape.
Land ho. Said with mild enthusiasm.
doldrums.enter: Welcome to the doldrums. Wind's on holiday. So's my patience.
The doldrums. Between the trade winds, nothing blows but me.
doldrums.exit: Trade wind again. Northeast up here, southeast down there. Reliable, unlike you.
round.start: New orders. Latitude's exact, direction's a shrug. Get to the latitude first, then run along it.
Sail north or south until the star says the right height. Then turn. That's the whole trick.
round.win: We found it. I'll be telling everyone I navigated.
Arrived. Somewhat on purpose. Well done.
Land, and the right land. Don't let it go to your head.
island.wrong: Wrong island. Compare the shape to the orders.
That's not it. Check your latitude.
tutorial.step7.intro: Here's a real job. There's an island north-east of us, and I know its latitude.
tutorial.step7.kamal: This is a kamal. Board on a string. Each knot is a port's latitude. Ancient, clever, cheap.
tutorial.step7.kamalHint: Press 2, hold right-click, look at Polaris. The board sits on the horizon for you.
tutorial.step7.kamalDone: Board on the horizon, star on the top edge. That's the whole instrument.
tutorial.step7.north: Head north. As we go, Polaris climbs. When it sits on the island's knot, we're on its latitude.
tutorial.step7.northHint: Keep north. Raise the kamal now and then. Star above the board's top edge: keep going.
tutorial.step7.northDone: Polaris is on the knot. We're on the island's latitude. Stop going north.
tutorial.step7.east: Now turn east and run along the latitude. This is how ships found islands for centuries.
tutorial.step7.eastHint: East is 090 on the compass. Steer with A and D. Gently.
tutorial.step7.done: Good. The island is somewhere ahead on this line. How far is the hard part.
tutorial.step8.intro: We don't know how far east it is. So we track speed and time. That's dead reckoning.
tutorial.step8.logHint: Press L. The log line counts knots while the sand runs. Yes, that's where knots come from.
tutorial.step8.logDone: Speed logged. Heading from the compass, speed from the log, time from the clock.
tutorial.step8.chart: Now the chart. Mark where we think we are. Thinking is generous.
tutorial.step8.chartHint: Let go of the wheel with E, walk to the table on the left, press E, click Mark position.
tutorial.step8.chartDone: Marked. Every error from here on is officially on record.
tutorial.step8.find: Back on course and keep the latitude. Islands hide in haze until you're close.
tutorial.step8.findHint: I've pencilled it on the chart. Just this once. Stay on the latitude and keep east.
tutorial.step8.done: Land, right where the star said. You'll take the credit. I'll allow it.
tutorial.step10.intro: You can find north, measure latitude and run it down. That's more than most captains.
tutorial.step10.done: No more hints. You're on your own. Try not to embarrass me.
